title: Monitoring storage
subtitle: Filesystem space, open files, and disk I/O load

cards.front: df vs du vs lsof vs iostat / vmstat -d
cards.meaning: df = disks; du = folders; lsof = who has it open; iostat / vmstat -d = how hard the disk is working
cards.notes: Space, who holds the file, and I/O busyness

cards.meaning: Free space per mounted filesystem, human-readable (G, M)
cards.notes: One row per mount: Size / Used / Avail / Use% / Mounted on

cards.meaning: Percent of the filesystem in use — what paging systems watch
cards.notes: Alert on Use%, not only Avail. df -h = "is / full?"

cards.front: df does not tell which directory ate space
cards.meaning: df shows mount free space; du finds which folder inside is fat
cards.notes: df = which mount; du -sh dir/* = which folder inside it

cards.meaning: Disk usage: one human-readable total per /etc/* entry
cards.notes: Typical hunt: du -sh /* then du -sh /var/* until you find the fat directory

cards.meaning: Summarize — one total per argument, not every nested file
cards.notes: Pair with -h for human sizes

cards.meaning: Human-readable sizes
cards.notes: Usually combined with -s

cards.meaning: Does not shrink du until the process closes it — then use lsof
cards.notes: Space held by a deleted-but-still-open file

cards.meaning: Lists open files belonging to active processes (files, dirs, sockets, devices)
cards.notes: On Linux everything is a file. Need root to see other users' files

cards.meaning: All open files, all processes (huge — page it)
cards.notes: No options = everything

cards.meaning: Processes that have this path open (e.g. the binary)
cards.notes: Path-based filter

cards.meaning: Open files for processes whose command name starts with sshd
cards.notes: -c = command name. Memory hook: -c nginx = that program

cards.meaning: Internet network files — TCP/UDP connections (who is listening / connected)
cards.notes: Also HP-UX x.25 network files per the notes

cards.meaning: Deleted-but-still-open files holding space (mentioned for later)
cards.notes: Memory hook from theory for the deleted-file space case

cards.meaning: Per-disk read/write statistics (totals, merged ops, sectors, time, current IO)
cards.notes: Each device like sda, dm-0. Memory hook: -d = each disk

cards.meaning: Detailed statistics about one partition (reads, sectors, writes, requested writes)
cards.notes: Memory hook: -p name = one partition

cards.meaning: Monitors and reports system I/O device loading (from sysstat)
cards.notes: Like sar / mpstat — same package family

cards.meaning: I/O load with timestamp; CPU averages and Device table
cards.notes: Memory hook: iostat -t = time + CPU + disks

cards.meaning: Device I/O only — no CPU block (tps, kB/s read/write)
cards.notes: Memory hook: iostat -d = disks only

cards.meaning: Live device samples: every 1 second, 5 times
cards.notes: Same interval/count idea as sar / vmstat

cards.meaning: Transfers (I/O requests) per second
cards.notes: Watch tps together with iowait and df

cards.meaning: Read / write throughput in kilobytes per second
cards.notes: Rate columns

cards.meaning: Total kilobytes read/written since boot (if no interval)
cards.notes: Cumulative counters without a live interval

cards.meaning: Often an LVM mapper sitting on a disk like sda — similar numbers expected
cards.notes: Mapper device, not a separate physical disk
